children: , the global oncology and biopharmaceutical powerhouse, delivered another Phase 3 victory Tuesday, with its stock priced at $161.62. Tagrisso combined with Hutchmed's Orpathys significantly delayed disease progression compared with Tagrisso alone in previously untreated patients with advanced lung cancer.

The SANOVO trial focused on tumors showing moderate-to-high MET protein expression, while overall-survival findings also looked encouraging. This follows another late-stage win for the same combination in patients whose cancer had already progressed on Tagrisso. Oncology generates nearly half of AstraZeneca's revenue, making every Tagrisso expansion critical to its $80 billion annual-sales target for 2030.

Here is the real prize: AstraZeneca is fighting to keep Tagrisso at the center of lung-cancer treatment even when tumors develop new resistance mechanisms. At $161.62, the stock trades 10.79% below its $181.17 GF Value estimate, suggesting the market is not pricing the business at full historical value. But the company has not revealed the size of SANOVO's clinical benefit, and the China-based results still need detailed data and regulatory support before the combination can meaningfully widen Tagrisso's commercial moat.

title: AstraZeneca's $80 Billion Plan Gets Another Tagrisso Win
